correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the result on the precise affine family. The one-sided images yield all-ones rows except for deletion of the first column after a -,+ turn or of the last column after a +,- turn. Nonempty open-cell paths are realizable by backward affine pullback; the cylinder entropy is the logarithm of the Perron root. With A,B the two turn counts and with z_0 normalized to one, the first row gives sum(z)=lambda and the last row gives r=z_last=1, 1-1/lambda or lambda/(lambda+1). The remaining rows reconstruct a positive eigenvector for the unique root of lambda(n-lambda)=A+B r on [n-1,n] for n>=3: the left-minus-right side has opposite weak endpoint signs and is strictly decreasing. Specializing the turn counts yields the three equations, and choosing the preterminal flip positions gives the binomial counts. For n=2 the constant words give radius 2; the two nonconstant radii are 1 and the golden ratio in the stated order. For n>=3 the alternating scores are at least n-1-floor(n/2)/(n-1)>n-2, whereas every nonalternator scores at most n-2. The negative-start advantage at fixed lambda is (lambda-m+1)/(lambda(lambda+1)) for n=2m and m/(lambda(lambda+1)) for n=2m+1; a larger score gives a strictly smaller root. Only zero flips achieve radius n. Writing its worst root as n-1+a gives (n-2)a+a^2=1/2+O(1/n), so a=1/(2n)+O(n^-2) and the n^-2 term in log(n/lambda) cancels. For all words, Delta=n-lambda satisfies n Delta-kappa=Delta^2-B(1-r), a difference of quantities in [0,1]; the log remainder gives the claimed uniform bound. The word-to-first-sign-and-flips bijection gives independent fair bits and fixes both the variance 1/4 and negligible centering correction in the CLT. Read the frozen checker but did not execute it: its one-winner update does not itself rule out ties, and its determinant checks are finite evaluations only. The analytic strict comparison and root proof supply what that diagnostic cannot. Replay: RESULT.md, Steps 1–5, with Oliveira Theorems 7.1–7.2 for the canonical premises.
